mainTopic: The גיד הנשה: why birds are exempt, which fat שמואל says everyone permits, whether the Torah forbids the main nerve or its branches, and the strands and white fat of the kidney.
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a list from the previous עמוד: three good things the nations of the world still keep. The גמרא then returns to the משנה. It explains that birds are exempt from גיד הנשה because their thigh bulge is not rounded. רבי ירמיה asks about a creature that breaks its species' pattern, and that question ends in תיקו. Next, שמואל says the משנה's words 'its fat is permitted' are agreed by everyone. The גמרא asks which fat he means. It rejects the fetus's fat, which רבי מאיר forbids, and concludes he meant the fat around the גיד, which רבי מאיר forbids only מדרבנן, as shown from two ברייתות. רב and עולא then argue whether the Torah forbade the main גיד or only its thin branches, and אביי supports עולא from the strands inside חלב. Finally, the גמרא discusses the white fat of the kidney. אביי begins a proof from שמואל for רבי אסי's lenient practice, and the proof continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The last three good practices the nations still keep
steps.stepSummary: The list ends: the nations do not write a כתובה for a marriage between men, do not sell human flesh in butcher shops, and they honor the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...that they do not write a marriage contract for males, and one is that they do not weigh the flesh of the dead in butcher shops, and one is that they honor the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a statement from the previous עמוד, which listed three things the nations still keep. Here we read the three items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even where people break a law in private, they still keep some public limits. They do not formalize forbidden relationships with a כתובה, they do not openly sell human flesh, and they still respect the תורה. These are the three points of merit on the list.
steps.whatToRemember: The list ends with three things the nations keep: no כתובה for men, no public sale of human flesh, and honoring the תורה.

phrases.english: that they do not write a marriage contract for males,
and one: that they do not weigh
the flesh of the dead in butcher shops,
and one: that they honor the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a statement that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three practices the nations still keep are: no כתובה for males, no public sale of human flesh, and honoring the תורה.

steps.title: But birds do seem to have the right thigh shape
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that גיד הנשה does not apply to birds, then asks: we can see that birds do have that thigh feature.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And it does not apply to a bird.' But we see that a bird does have it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which says the גיד הנשה law does not apply to birds. It then challenges this from what we can see with our own eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts birds because the פסוק speaks of the 'כף הירך' (the spoon-shaped bulge of the thigh), and birds supposedly lack it. The challenge is that birds clearly have a bulge on the thigh. If they have it, why should they be exempt?

keyTerms.meaning: But we see! (a challenge from what we can observe)

phrases.english: And it does not apply to a bird.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which says a bird has no 'spoon of the thigh' (בראשית 32:33).

phrases.english: But we see that it does have it?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the thigh bulge the פסוק talks about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: back to the משנה about גיד הנשה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that birds lack the כף הירך.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We can observe a thigh bulge on birds, so the reason for exempting them seems false.

steps.title: A bird's thigh bulge is not rounded
steps.stepSummary: Birds do have a bulge, but it is not rounded like the כף הירך the פסוק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: It has a bulge, but it is not rounded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Yes, birds have a bulge, but it is the wrong shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'spoon' of the thigh must be rounded. A bird's bulge is flat, not round, so it does not count. That is why birds are exempt.

phrases.english: It has it, but it is not rounded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the requirement more exactly: the bulge must be rounded.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any thigh bulge counts as a כף הירך, so birds should be included.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a rounded bulge counts. A bird's bulge is not rounded, so birds are exempt.

steps.title: What about an unusual bird or an unusual animal?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about a bird that does have a rounded bulge, or an animal that does not. Do we follow the individual creature or its species?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: if a bird has a rounded bulge, or an animal has a bulge that is not rounded, what is the law? Do we go by this particular creature, or by its species?
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the last answer, רבי ירמיה asks about exceptions to the normal pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the rounded shape is what matters. So what happens when a single creature does not match its kind? Either we judge each creature by its own body, or we judge by what is normal for its species. In the second case, animals are always included and birds are always exempt.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
if a bird has it and it is rounded,

phrases.aramaic: אִית לֵיהּ לִבְהֵמָה וְלָא עֲגִיל, מַאי?
phrases.english: or an animal has it and it is not rounded, what is the law?
Do we follow it itself,
or do we follow its species?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 'rounded' answer from step 3 to ask about unusual cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the גיד הנשה law depends on the individual creature's shape or on what is normal for its species.

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רבי ירמיה's question with תיקו: no answer is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot settle רבי ירמיה's question, so it closes the discussion with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides whether we follow the individual or the species. The question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'no' or 'yes'. It means the גמרא found no answer either way.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from step 4 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether we follow the individual creature or its species stays undecided.

steps.title: שמואל: 'its fat is permitted' is agreed by everyone
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says גיד הנשה applies to a fetus, while רבי יהודה disagrees and adds 'and its fat is permitted.' שמואל says that this permission of 'its fat' is agreed by all. The next steps work out which fat he means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And it applies to a fetus.' שמואל said: 'And its fat is permitted' is according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about a שליל (a fetus inside its mother). שמואל explains whose opinion the words 'its fat is permitted' follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the תנא קמא holds that גיד הנשה applies to a fetus. רבי יהודה says it does not, and adds that its fat is permitted. שמואל says the words 'its fat is permitted' are agreed by everyone. The word 'its' is unclear, and the next steps ask whether it means the fetus's fat or the fat of the גיד.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus still inside its mother
The forbidden fats of an animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'its fat' means the fetus's fat. The גמרא rejects that reading in step 8 and concludes that שמואל meant the fat around the גיד.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's short statement opens the whole discussion that follows. The גמרא works out which 'fat' he meant and in what sense everyone permits it.

phrases.english: And it applies to a fetus.
Shmuel said:
'And its fat is permitted'
is according to everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְחֶלְבּוֹ מוּתָּר לְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Its fat is permitted' is agreed by everyone. The גמרא later explains this refers to the fat of the גיד, permitted מן התורה.

steps.title: Which fat did שמואל mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'its fat' in שמואל's statement refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The fat of what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which fat שמואל was talking about when he said everyone agrees it is permitted. This question sets up the next two attempts to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said 'its fat is permitted' according to all, but 'its' is unclear. It could be the fat of the fetus or the fat around the גיד הנשה. Each option will be checked against known disagreements.

phrases.english: Its fat — the fat of what?
phrases.notes: This goes back to שמואל's statement in the last step, that 'its fat is permitted' according to everyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the key word in שמואל's statement from step 6 refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שמואל meant the fat of the שליל or the fat of the גיד הנשה.

steps.title: It cannot mean the fetus's fat, since that is disputed
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל meant the fat of a שליל, a ברייתא shows רבי מאיר forbids it, so it is not agreed by all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he meant the fat of a fetus, the תנאים argue about that. A ברייתא teaches: the law of גיד הנשה applies to a fetus and its fat is forbidden, says רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says it does not apply to a fetus and its fat is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option, that שמואל meant the fat of a fetus, and rejects it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said 'everyone agrees.' But this ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר forbids the fetus's fat. So that cannot be what שמואל meant.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (trying out a possible answer)
A fetus found inside a slaughtered animal

phrases.english: If you say it means the fat of a fetus
but they disagree about it!
As a ברייתא teaches: it applies to a fetus,
and its fat is forbidden; these are the words of רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג בַּשְּׁלִיל,
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: it does not apply to a fetus,
and its fat is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא דִּשְׁלִיל וְהָא מִיפְלָג פְּלִיגִי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to step 7 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the fat is agreed by all, if read as the fat of a שליל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר forbids a שליל's fat, so it is not agreed by all.

steps.title: The fetus dispute is a real disagreement
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא explains that the ברייתא's argument is about a live full-term fetus. Each תנא follows his usual view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: the disagreement is about a live nine-month fetus. רבי מאיר follows his usual view, and רבי יהודה follows his usual view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds an explanation of the ברייתא. It shows the argument about the fetus is a real, built-in disagreement, which makes the question from step 8 stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a full-term fetus that is still alive after its mother was slaughtered. רבי מאיר treats it as its own animal, so its fat is forbidden. רבי יהודה treats it as part of the mother, so its fat is permitted. The argument comes from their basic views, so it cannot be explained away.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his own usual view

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: And רבי אלעזר said that רבי אושעיא said:
The dispute is about a live nine-month fetus,
phrases.notes: This is a fetus found still alive after its mother was slaughtered.

phrases.english: and רבי מאיר follows his usual view,
and רבי יהודה follows his usual view.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the question in step 8 by showing the disagreement is real and built into each תנא's basic view.
steps.raayaObject: That the fat of a שליל is truly disputed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אושעיא's explanation of the ברייתא.

steps.title: The fat of the גיד is also disputed
steps.stepSummary: If שמואל meant the fat around the גיד הנשה, another ברייתא shows רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about that too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then maybe he meant the fat of the גיד? But they argue about that too. A ברייתא teaches: with the גיד הנשה, one digs after it wherever it is and cuts its fat out from the root; these are רבי מאיר's words. רבי יהודה says: one cuts it level with the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option, that שמואל meant the fat around the גיד הנשה. It challenges this with another ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר requires removing all the fat, even the parts deep in the meat. רבי יהודה only requires cutting it level with the surface. So it seems the fat of the גיד is also not agreed by all.

keyTerms.meaning: Its fat (the fat around the גיד)
Cuts it level, trims it off

phrases.english: Rather, the fat of the גיד?
But they disagree about that too!
As a ברייתא teaches: the גיד הנשה, one digs after it
wherever it is,
and cuts out its fat from its root
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: גּוֹמְמוֹ עִם הַשּׁוֹפִי.
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: one cuts it level with the surface of the meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא חֶלְבּוֹ דְּגִיד הָא מִיפְלָג פְּלִיגִי בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first option failed, so the גמרא tries the second option and attacks it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the fat is agreed by all, if read as the fat of the גיד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר requires removing all the fat around the גיד, which seems to show he forbids it.

steps.title: He meant the fat of the גיד, and רבי מאיר forbids it only מדרבנן
steps.stepSummary: שמואל did mean the fat of the גיד. רבי מאיר's strictness is only a rabbinic law, so מן התורה everyone permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he meant the fat of the גיד. שמואל agrees that according to רבי מאיר it is forbidden by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל did mean the fat of the גיד. רבי מאיר forbids it only מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's 'everyone agrees it is permitted' is about Torah law. רבי מאיר's demand to remove all the fat is only a rabbinic stricture. So it does not contradict שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (going back to the option that was rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי מאיר holds this fat is forbidden by the Torah. Here he forbids it only מדרבנן, which is why שמואל can still say everyone permits it.

phrases.english: Really, it is the fat of the גיד,
and שמואל agrees that according to רבי מאיר
it is forbidden by rabbinic law,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10 by limiting רבי מאיר's ruling to rabbinic law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting Torah law from rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's requirement to remove all the fat means he holds it is forbidden by the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר forbids it only מדרבנן, so מן התורה it is permitted according to everyone.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports this: Torah-permitted, but the Jewish people are strict
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the fat is permitted, but holy Jews treat it as forbidden. The גמרא suggests this is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: its fat is permitted, but the holy Jewish people treat it as forbidden. Is this not רבי מאיר, who says it is permitted by the Torah and forbidden by rabbinic law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support its answer, that the fat of the גיד is permitted by the Torah and forbidden only by custom or rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the fat is permitted, yet Jews are strict about it. The גמרא suggests this matches רבי מאיר, who requires removing the fat but only מדרבנן. This backs up the answer in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Treated it as forbidden (a custom of strictness)
Is it not that...? (introduces a suggested proof)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's 'its fat is permitted according to all' means the fat of the גיד הנשה, and it is about Torah law. רבי מאיר forbids it only מדרבנן, and Jews keep the strict custom.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for treating the fat around the גיד הנשה as forbidden in practice. It is permitted by the Torah, but the holy Jewish people are strict about it.

phrases.english: As a ברייתא teaches: and its fat is permitted,
but the Jewish people are holy and treated it as forbidden.
Is it not רבי מאיר's view,
who said: it is permitted by Torah law
and forbidden by rabbinic law?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא וְשׇׁמְנוֹ מוּתָּר וְיִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים נָהֲגוּ בּוֹ אִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the answer given in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי מאיר, the fat of the גיד is permitted by the Torah and forbidden only by rabbinic law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: 'its fat is permitted, but the holy Jewish people treated it as forbidden.'

steps.title: Maybe that ברייתא follows רבי יהודה instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion from Step 12. Maybe the ברייתא ('the fat is permitted, but holy Jews forbid it') is רבי יהודה, and רבי מאיר forbids the fat מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe that ברייתא is רבי יהודה's view, but according to רבי מאיר the fat is forbidden even by Torah law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion that the 'holy Jews' ברייתא is רבי מאיר. Maybe it is really רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 claimed that רבי מאיר's strictness is only rabbinic, and Step 12 used the 'holy Jews' ברייתא as support. If that ברייתא is really רבי יהודה, the support is gone. Then רבי מאיר could forbid the fat מן התורה, and שמואל's 'everyone agrees' would fail again.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do you know?
By Torah law (as opposed to rabbinic law)

phrases.english: From where [do you know this]?
Perhaps it is the view of Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא from the last step that says holy Jews treat the fat as forbidden.

phrases.english: but according to Rabbi Meir
it is forbidden even by Torah law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification made in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'holy Jews' ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא could just as easily be רבי יהודה, which leaves open that רבי מאיר forbids the fat מן התורה.

steps.title: Proof that רבי מאיר permits the fat by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. A ברייתא requires scraping out the גיד completely, which is רבי מאיר's view, and it says the fat is permitted. So רבי מאיר permits the fat מן התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That can't be, as a ברייתא teaches: one scrapes out the גיד הנשה wherever it is, and its fat is permitted. Who requires scraping? רבי מאיר. And the ברייתא says its fat is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a new ברייתא. It shows that רבי מאיר himself says the fat is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא requires חטיטה, scraping the nerve out even where it is hidden deep in the meat. Only רבי מאיר holds this, so the ברייתא is his. Since it also says 'its fat is permitted,' רבי מאיר must permit the fat מן התורה. His strictness is only rabbinic, which saves the answer of Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: It would not enter your mind; that cannot be
Scraping or digging out, removing the nerve completely from every place it runs

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, the fat of the גיד הנשה is permitted מן התורה. His strictness about it is only rabbinic, so שמואל's statement that everyone agrees holds up.

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
The sciatic nerve: one scrapes around after it
in every place where it is,
phrases.notes: This means you have to dig it out completely, even the parts that run deep inside the meat.

phrases.english: and its fat is permitted.
Whom have you heard
who holds that scraping is required?
Rabbi Meir.
And it says: its fat is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of Step 13 with a proof from a ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a source that identifies the author
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'holy Jews' ברייתא might be רבי יהודה, and רבי מאיר might forbid the fat מן התורה
steps.terutzMaskana: A ברייתא that follows רבי מאיר (it requires חטיטה) says the fat is permitted, so רבי מאיר permits it מן התורה
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's view on the fat of the גיד
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא requiring חטיטה that also says שמנו מותר

steps.title: רב: the Torah forbade only the thin branches of the גיד
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens. רב says that the Torah forbids only the thin branch-strands (קנוקנות) of the גיד הנשה, not the main nerve.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא said in the name of רב: The Torah forbade only the thin branches of the גיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new discussion about what exactly is forbidden in the גיד הנשה. רב says only the thin branches are forbidden מן התורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main גיד הנשה is hard and tasteless, like wood, so רב holds it is not food and the Torah prohibition does not apply to it. The prohibition falls on the thin strands that branch off from it inside the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Thin, tendril-like branches that come off the main nerve
The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids eating

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying the branches are a small extra on top of the main nerve. He says the Torah prohibition itself is on the branches, because the main nerve, being like wood, is not considered food.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta said
that Rav said:
The Torah did not forbid
anything except its thin branches.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about which part of the גיד is forbidden
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah prohibition of גיד הנשה applies only to its קנוקנות

steps.title: עולא: the גיד is like wood, but the Torah made it forbidden
steps.stepSummary: עולא disagrees with רב. The main גיד is like wood, but the Torah still makes one liable for eating it.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is wood, but the Torah made one liable for it.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives the opposing view to רב. He says the main nerve itself is forbidden even though it is like wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא agrees with רב that the main nerve has no taste, like wood. But he holds that this is exactly what the Torah forbade, a special rule even though it is not normal food. So the main nerve carries Torah liability.

keyTerms.meaning: It is wood; it is tasteless and not normal food
Made one liable for eating it

phrases.english: Ulla said:
It is wood,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the main גיד הנשה. It is so hard and tasteless that it is like eating wood.

phrases.english: but the Torah made one liable for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר: עֵץ הוּא, וְהַתּוֹרָה חִיְּיבָה עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב in Step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main גיד הנשה, though like wood, is forbidden by the Torah

steps.title: אביי supports עולא from the strands inside חלב
steps.stepSummary: אביי says עולא's view makes more sense. Strands inside forbidden fat are forbidden, but there is no Torah liability for them, because the Torah said 'חלב' and not strands. In the same way, the Torah said 'גיד' and not the branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It makes sense to follow עולא. רב ששת said in the name of רב אסי: Strands in the חלב are forbidden, but one is not liable for them. So the Torah said 'fat' and not strands. Here too, the Torah said 'nerve' and not the branches.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a proof to back up עולא against רב. He compares the branches of the גיד to the strands inside חלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי teaches that the Torah prohibition is on the main item it names (חלב), not on the thin strands inside it. Those strands are only forbidden rabbinically. By the same logic, the Torah named the 'גיד', so the main nerve carries Torah liability and the thin branches do not. This is the opposite of רב's view and supports עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes sense
Thin strands of veins found inside forbidden fat
Forbidden, but with no Torah punishment (only rabbinic)
The Merciful One; a name for ה׳ used when quoting the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: אביי holds like עולא: the Torah's prohibition is on the main גיד itself, just as the prohibition of חלב is on the fat itself and not on the strands inside it.
steps.whyThisMatters: אביי's support for עולא is a comparison, not a general rule: strands inside חלב are forbidden but carry no Torah liability, because the Torah said 'חלב' and not the strands - and in the same way the Torah said 'גיד', so its branches are outside Torah liability. Whether the branches are forbidden in practice is a separate question.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It stands to reason to follow Ulla,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: as Rav Sheshet said that Rav Asi said:
The strands that are in the forbidden fat are forbidden,
but one is not liable for eating them.
Apparently, the Merciful One said "fat"
and not strands.
Here too, the Merciful One said "nerve"
and not the thin branches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports עולא in Step 16 against רב in Step 15
steps.raayaObject: עולא's view that the main גיד carries Torah liability
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אסי's rule that חוטין שבחלב are forbidden but carry no Torah liability

steps.title: Strands in the fat and kidney, and the argument about the kidney's white fat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the statement it quoted earlier. רב אסי rules that strands in the חלב and in the kidney are forbidden, but there is no Torah liability for them. רבי and רבי חייא argue about the white fat of the kidney.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself: רב ששת said in the name of רב אסי: The strands inside the forbidden fat are forbidden, but you are not liable for eating them. The strands inside the kidney are forbidden, but you are not liable for eating them. As for the white fat of the kidney, רבי and רבי חייא argue: one forbids it and one permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quote in full the statement of רב אסי that אביי used as his proof in Step 17. Now we see the whole statement, including a new part about the kidney.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 used only the first line, about strands in the חלב. The full statement adds that strands in the כוליא are treated the same way: forbidden, but with no Torah liability. It also adds a new argument about לובן כוליא, the white fat inside the kidney's groove.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא goes back to discuss a statement it quoted earlier in passing
Strands, small veins or threads running through the meat
Forbidden to eat, but with no Torah punishment for eating them
The white fat inside the kidney's groove, spreading into the kidney itself

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forbidden but not liable' does not mean permitted. You still may not eat these strands. It only means there is no Torah punishment for eating them.

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav Sheshet said that Rav Asi said:
phrases.notes: This is the statement אביי relied on just before. Now the גמרא quotes all of it.

phrases.english: The strands that are in the forbidden fat are forbidden,
but one is not liable for eating them.
Those that are in the kidney are forbidden,
phrases.notes: 'Those' means the strands again, this time the ones inside the kidney.

phrases.english: but one is not liable for eating them.
The white fat of the kidney:
Rabbi and Rabbi Ḥiyya argue:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name always means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: one forbids it, and one permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the source אביי quoted in Step 17 and presents it in full
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Strands in the חלב and in the כוליא are forbidden but carry no Torah liability. The white fat of the kidney is disputed between רבי and רבי חייא.

steps.title: How different sages removed the kidney's white fat
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רבי יוחנן scraped away the white fat of the kidney completely. רבי אסי only cut it off the surface.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה would scrape it out. רבי יוחנן would scrape it out. רבי אסי would just cut it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how three אמוראים actually handled the white fat of the kidney in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scraping removes every last bit of the white fat, which is the strict way. Cutting removes only what sits on the surface and leaves the rest. So רבי אסי treated the fat inside the kidney more leniently than רבה and רבי יוחנן did.

keyTerms.meaning: Scrapes or peels away completely, leaving nothing behind
Cuts off, trims only from the surface

phrases.english: Rabba would scrape it away,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the white fat of the kidney from the line before.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan would scrape it away,
Rabbi Asi would cut it off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the argument about לובן כוליא played out in actual practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה and רבי יוחנן scraped out all the white fat. רבי אסי only cut it from the surface.

steps.title: אביי sides with רבי אסי and begins his proof
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי אסי's practice makes the most sense. He starts bringing a proof from שמואל, and the proof continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It makes sense to follow רבי אסי, because רבי אבא said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל:
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes a side and says רבי אסי's lighter way of cutting is correct. This line is setting up the next move: the actual proof from שמואל comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is not just giving an opinion. He is about to back it up with a ruling from שמואל. We must wait for the next lines to see how שמואל's words support cutting rather than scraping.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with him, following his opinion
It makes sense, it stands to reason

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי מִסְתַּבְּרָא,
phrases.english: Abaye said: It stands to reason to follow Rabbi Asi,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: because Rabbi Abba said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the practices described in Step 19 and starts to bring a source
steps.raayaObject: That cutting off the white fat, as רבי אסי did, is enough
steps.raayaSupportSource: A statement of שמואל, passed down through רב יהודה and רבי אבא, which is quoted in the continuation
